digest.top_line: RAVES QoL: adjuvant fossa RT drives 16% vs 2% severe urinary leakage at 5yr, with no QOL penalty for delaying to salvage.
digest.tldr: The prostate day is a toxicity read, not an efficacy one: RAVES's QoL substudy prices the cost of treating everyone up front, 16% vs 2% severe urinary leakage at 5yr, while aRT vs sRT-who-actually-got-RT is a wash (16% vs 13%, p=0.7). Time from RP to RT tracked with nothing, so early salvage carries no QOL tax.

sites.intro: Post-RP fossa RT: the QOL argument for salvage over adjuvant rests on the half of pts who never need RT, not on any per-patient toxicity advantage.

studies.name: TROG 08.03 RAVES (QoL substudy)
studies.tldr: Severe urinary leakage 16% vs 2% at 5yr with aRT vs no RT; sRT timing had no QOL association.

details.text: 📊 1° EP: MCIC (>0.5 SD decline from baseline) per EORTC QLQ-PR25 domain

details: 🔍 Planned secondary analysis of the phase 3 non-inferiority RAVES trial; n=166 aRT, n=167 sRT
🔍 RT was 64 Gy/32 fx to the prostate fossa in both arms; concurrent ADT and pelvic nodal RT not allowed

details.text: 📐 Only 80/167 (48%) of sRT-arm pts ever received RT; median time to sRT 2.6 yr (IQR 1.5-4.6)
📊 Bowel MCIC at 5yr, aRT 37% (40/109) vs no-RT 12% (6/50); vs full sRT arm 37% vs 20%, p=0.009
📊 Severe ("quite a bit"/"very much") urinary leakage, aRT vs no RT
📊 aRT vs sRT-who-received-RT: severe urinary leakage at 5yr 16% vs 13%, p=0.7

details: 📐 Time from RP to RT showed no association with any domain at 3-5 yr (all univariable coefficients ns, Table 2)

details.text: ⚠️ Bowel MCIC threshold was a 2-point change on a 100-point scale, a minor worsening by the authors' own reading

details: ⚠️ Most pts treated with 3D-CRT, not IMRT; modern planning would be expected to lower the bowel signal
⚠️ Exploratory, no correction for multiple testing; 5yr QOL completion only 64% (214/333)
⚠️ sRT-arm pts who received RT had worse sexual activity MCIC at 3yr (58% vs 32%, p=0.004) and 4yr (65% vs 43%, p=0.038), confounded by higher-risk disease and likely ADT
🔗 Clinician-rated toxicity in the parent RAVES: G2+ GU 70% aRT vs 54% sRT, with no GI difference, so the patient-reported bowel signal here is the discrepant finding

verdict.rationale: Protocol-planned secondary QOL analysis of a randomized trial; supports the already-guideline-endorsed early sRT strategy. Exploratory, unadjusted for multiplicity, so not independently practice-setting.
verdict.audience: Post-RP prostate ca with adverse pathology (+margin, EPE, or SVI), Gleason 7 in…

studies.significance: The QOL argument for salvage is about avoidance, not delay: 52% of the sRT arm never needed RT, and among men who did get RT, aRT vs sRT differed by 16% vs 13% severe leakage at 5yr (p=0.7). With 64 Gy/32 fx 3D-CRT, no ADT, no nodal RT, this does not license waiting once PSA rises.
studies.monday_clinic: In a man with adverse pathology after RP and an undetectable PSA, this supports observing to early salvage rather than adjuvant RT on QOL grounds; it does not speak to Gleason 9 pts needing ADT or pelvic nodal coverage, who were not represented here.

primary_endpoint.name: Minimal clinically important change (MCIC) in EORTC QLQ-PR25 domains
primary_endpoint.stat_value: Severe urinary leakage 16% vs 2% at 5 yr

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Protocol-planned secondary analysis of the TROG 08.03 RAVES phase 3 noninferiority trial. **Primary end point here: MCIC**, defined as a **>0.5 SD decline** from mean baseline on each EORTC QLQ-PR25 domain, with chi-square testing at each year. Median follow-up 6 yr in both arms (IQR 4-7.1).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: 333 men randomized after RP with **adverse pathology** (positive margins, extraprostatic extension, or seminal vesicle invasion): 166 aRT, 167 sRT. **Gleason 7 in 82%**, Gleason 8 in 3%, Gleason 9 in 12%. Median age 63.8 vs 63.9 yr (p=0.9).

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **64 Gy in 32 fractions to the prostate fossa** in both arms, mostly **3D-CRT rather than IMRT**. aRT within 6 mo of RP; sRT triggered at **PSA >0.2 ng/ml** and delivered within 4 mo. **Concurrent ADT and pelvic nodal RT were prohibited**, so this is an RT-alone toxicity read.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: **Only 48% (80/167) of the sRT arm ever received RT.** Bowel MCIC at 5 yr was 37% (40/109) with aRT vs 12% (6/50) in men who never had RT, and 37% vs 20% (p=0.009) against the whole sRT arm. Against men who did receive salvage, **no consistent difference** in urinary, bowel, or sexual domains from 1 to 5 yr after RT.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Parent RAVES reported clinician-scored **G2+ GU toxicity 70% aRT vs 54% sRT** with no GI difference, the inverse pattern to the patient-reported bowel signal here. Historic clinician-rated **G2 incontinence of 10-20%** brackets the 16% severe leakage seen at 5 yr. Cross-comparison with GETUG-AFU 17 and RADICALS is limited by differing urinary grading.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents post-RP men with adverse pathology treated with conventionally fractionated fossa-only RT without ADT. Does not represent men needing pelvic nodal RT, concurrent ADT, hypofractionation (NRG-GU003), or salvage SBRT.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Bowel MCIC corresponded to a **2-point change on a 100-point scale**, one Likert step on one of four questions, so the 37% vs 12% gap may be a minor symptom shift rather than a functional one. The aRT-vs-received-sRT comparison is **non-randomized**: those men had higher-risk disease, were older at RT (66.8 vs 63.9, p=0.01), and more likely received ADT, which plausibly drives the sexual-activity difference. Comorbidities and medications were not modeled.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The avoidance, not the delay, is what protects QOL: 52% of the sRT arm never needed RT, while aRT vs received-sRT showed 16% vs 13% severe leakage at 5 yr (p=0.7) and flat regression coefficients for RP-to-RT interval. Delivered as 64 Gy/32 fx 3D-CRT with no ADT or nodal RT, so the bowel signal likely overstates what IMRT would produce.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: For counselling a man with a positive margin, EPE, or SVI at RP, deferring to PSA-triggered salvage spares about half of them any RT, and RT itself carried 16% vs 2% severe urinary leakage at 5 yr against never-irradiated men. Timing of salvage after surgery showed no QOL penalty, so the post-op conversation can center on surveillance intensity rather than urgency.
